It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (major shrine), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}} its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called “Nijō Shrine” and “Katsuragi ni imasu Futakami Shrine.” {{nihongo|'''Katsuragi Futakami Shrine'''|葛木二上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
It enshrines Toyofutsu-no-Mitama-no-Kami and {{ill|Kunitama|Q9692242|qid=Q9692242|lt=Ōkunitama-no-Kami}}. There is a tradition that Toyofutsu-no-Mitama-no-Kami was invited to {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|Q708859|qid=Q708859}} and Ōkunitama-no-Kami to {{ill|Ōyamato Shrine|abstract|Q245731|fr|Ōyamato-jinja|ja|大和神社|ru|Ооямато-дзиндзя|simple|Ōyamato Shrine|zh|大和神社|qid=Q245731}}. The name {{ill|Futsu-no-mitama|Q11059754|qid=Q11059754}} is well known for Toyofutsu-no-Mitama-no-Kami, but why “Toyo” is prefixed is unclear. He is also considered the same deity as {{ill|Takemikazuchi|de|Takemikazuchi|eo|Takemikazuĉi|es|Takemikazuchi|fa|تاکه‌میکازوچی|fr|Takemikazuchi|id|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|pl|Takemikazuchi|pt|Takemikadzuchi|ru|Такэмикадзути|zh|建御雷|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}. Ōkunitama-no-Kami is regarded as the great commander among the {{ill|Kunitsukami|Q60995523|qid=Q60995523}}.

''Jinja Yōroku'' records “Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto, Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto,” while ''Jingi-shi'' records “Ki Toyofutsu-no-Mitama-no-Kami, Ōkuni-no-Kami.” Originally, male and female deities are thought to have been enshrined separately on the two summits of Mount Nijō (male peak and female peak).

== History ==
The date and circumstances of foundation are unknown. Mount Nijō has layers of {{ill|Sanukitoid|Q843420|qid=Q843420}} used as raw material for {{ill|Stone tool|Q479257|qid=Q479257}}, and people are thought to have lived nearby since ancient times. The first documentary appearance is in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}} under {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), first month, day 27, where the shrine is granted the divine rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位|ko|종5위|zh|從五位|qid=Q11071125}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “Katsuragi Futakami Shrine, two seats, {{ill|Katsuge district|Q11620862|qid=Q11620862}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}},” and ranked as a major shrine.

The “Map of the Vicinity of Taima-dera” held by {{ill|Taima-dera|Q478979|qid=Q478979}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakanobō}} records that there was also a shrine to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinja Daiō}} ({{ill|Dragon King|Q135337914|qid=Q135337914}}) on the female peak of Mount Nijō; tradition says it was moved and is now a small Ryūō shrine under the Inari subsidiary shrine within Nakanobō’s precincts. Its relation to this shrine is unknown.

In the early modern period this shrine was called “Take no {{ill|Gongen|Q3080343|qid=Q3080343}},” and was the ujigami for several dozen villages in the Take-go region using water flow from Mount Nijō. It was ranked as gōsha in April 1873 (Meiji 6).

== Precincts ==
The current shrine building burned in the 1974 ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 49) major fire on Mount Nijō and was rebuilt in 1975; inside is a small sacred sakaki object. East of the main shrine is the tomb of {{ill|Prince Ōtsu|Q1284081|qid=Q1284081}}.

At {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuragi Shitatori ni imasu Amenohazuchi-no-Mikoto Shrine}} (Shitatori Shrine) at the mountain foot, Ōkunitama-no-Kami of this shrine is enshrined as an associated deity.

== Festivals ==
In drought years, villagers of Take-go would climb the mountain for rain prayer chanting “The god of the mountain loves banners, bring banners and let rain fall.” Today, volunteer “Take-nobori” climbs are held annually on April 23.

== Other ==
Entry to the precinct (male peak summit) requires paying a 200-yen environmental preservation cooperation fee to the shrine.
